transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-27 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jon Reyes (Product), Mark Rivera (CTO, Lighthouse), Dana Li (ML Eng), Omar Khan (Security), Sofia (PM)

Summary: quick walk-through of Redwood API and Optimize suggestions for migrating from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together. Focus on parity, cost, and security.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, uh AE on this account, Priya is our solutions eng and Jon is product. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Mark: Good thanks, hope you can help we're trying to tidy up a multi-vendor mess, cost is spiking, latency is variable, and compliance wants a clear path.
[00:12] Priya: Great, can you quickly confirm your current stack? I noted OpenAI for chat/generation, Anthropic for some safety-sensitive prompts, and Together for a couple of fine-tuned models. Is that right?
[00:20] Dana: Yes that's right. We run gpt-4o-ish endpoints with OpenAI, Claude for long-form safety checks, and Together hosts our internal tuned distil model for triage.
[00:29] Omar: from security i care about data residency, kms, audit logs, and SSO/SAML. We also need to know what lives in Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated/VPC for PHI in the future.
[00:38] Alex: Perfect. Today's agenda: short parity mapping overview, console tour focusing on routing and Optimize suggestions, then Q&A and next steps.

[00:45] Priya: For parity i want to highlight three things that typically differ across vendors: tokenization/delta in token counts, sampling defaults (temperature/stop sequences), and model behaviors on system prompts. We'll show how Redwood handles those and where you might tweak prompts or model variants.

[01:12] Mark: One immediate question — embeddings. Our semantic search relies on 1536-dim vectors from vendor X; how does Redwood match dims and distance functions?
[01:22] Jon: Good question. Redwood supports embeddings mapping and will surface model compatibility; we also support cosine and dot-prod and can remap or run a small transform. But there is usually a small drift — we recommend running an embedding parity test to measure MRR and then decide if you transform or re-index.

[01:50] Dana: Also, token billing differences — some vendors have different tokenizers so counts don't line up, how do you normalize cost comparisons?
[01:58] Priya: We provide a benchmark template that normalizes by raw character input, tokenizes across providers to show token delta, and reports per-token cost at typical prompt/response sizes. That's in the benchmark spreadsheet we'll share.

[02:25] [Priya shares console — brief pause, audible mouse clicks]
[02:30] Priya: Here's the Console. Top right is the routing policy. We can route by latency SLO, cost preference, or region. For example you can prefer cheaper quantized variants for background tasks and route high-priority traffic to a larger float model.
[02:48] Mark: Will that change responses? If i route to a quantized variant, is there a measurable quality drop?
[02:54] Priya: There can be; that's why Redwood Optimize recommends per-route model profiles and provides eval hooks to catch regressions. You can set automatic fallback to the float model if Rouge/QA metrics fall below threshold.

[03:20] [Jon interjects] Jon: Also note we support KV/prefix cache for repeated contexts, which reduces latency and token spend — useful for triage flows with stable instructions.

[03:38] [00:03:38] Dana: About streaming — we currently rely on streaming to show partial results in our UI. Does Redwood support chunked piped streaming and function/tool calling like openai's function calls?
[03:48] Priya: Yes, streaming with chunked tokens and function-calling semantics are supported. Small differences: we encode function outputs in the same structured format, but there are subtle differences in how tool arguments are coerced. We added an adapter layer in the SDK to make swapping easier.

[04:12] Omar: Security: where do keys live, how is KMS integrated? Our compliance requires customer-managed keys for PHI.
[04:20] Alex: For Redwood Private/Dedicated we offer KMS integrations and can bring-your-own-key with HSM-backed providers. Hosted API can also integrate with enterprise KMS under certain plans. We'll send the security pack with SOC2/ISO and our KMS patterns.

[04:42] Mark: latency. Our triage path targets sub-120ms median for 64-token ops. Can you get that on Redwood hosted or do we need Dedicated?
[04:52] Priya: For sub-120ms medians on generation you'll likely need Dedicated or edge-optimized instances with pinned capacity depending on QPS. Redwood's routing can fallback to cheaper pools but for strict SLOs Dedicated is the safest route. We'll run a bench and show the trade-offs.

[05:20] Dana: Are there any gotchas converting prompts with stop sequences and system instructions from Anthropic's style to Redwood API?
[05:28] Priya: Anthropic's assistant/system split maps to Redwood system messages; stop sequences need translation sometimes. We find most teams do a quick pass of system prompts and keep user prompts identical. We documented common transformations in the migration playbook.

[05:50] [Speaker 3 unintelligible]
[05:55] Mark: About deployments — we want eventually to host in our VPC for PHI and regulatory reasons but start with hosted pilot. How long to move from hosted to a VPC private deployment?
[06:03] Alex: Typical flow: 2–4 week hosted pilot, then Dedicated/VPC provisioning takes 4–8 weeks depending on network reviews and onboarding. For on-prem there is more lead time. We can also set up a hybrid where critical routes go to VPC and background routes remain hosted.

[06:30] Priya: Demo time — i'll run a quick parity example. We'll take a sample triage prompt, show outputs from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together (we have synthetic examples) then show Redwood's response and explain differences.

[06:45] [Demo audio — typing]
[07:00] Priya: Example 1: triage summary generation. OpenAI version includes slightly longer hallucinated details, Anthropic is more conservative, Together (tuned) is terse. Redwood with model X-3b-quant gives a middle ground; if you pin X-8b-float we get longer, more detailed responses.

[07:32] Dana: So for parity do you recommend preserving the tuned Together model or retraining on Redwood?
[07:40] Priya: Two lanes: adapter pattern (keep your tuned weights on Together and use Redwood as runtime adapter) or port the tuning to a Redwood-verified base and re-run finetune. Adapter is faster but can incur runtime orchestration. Porting gives more stable long-term ops.

[08:05] Mark: Cost math — our bill today is a mix of per-token and per-hour infra — can you help make a clear ROI for a pilot?
[08:14] Jon: We'll provide a benchmark that shows per-request median latency, token usage normalized, and projected monthly cost at your QPS. Redwood Optimize will recommend batching thresholds and quantization levels to cut token spend 20-40% for background tasks.

[08:35] Omar: About audit logs — we need immutable logs for every request and redaction options for PHI in logs.
[08:44] Alex: Audit logs are supported — request/response metadata, routing decision, model version. For PHI we support configurable redaction and can integrate with your SIEM. We'll share log retention and export options in the security pack.

[09:05] [Short pause]
[09:12] Sofia: Timelines — if we start a pilot this week what's realistic?
[09:18] Alex: Start hosted pilot in 1 week, 2–4 weeks to gather meaningful benchmarks, security review in parallel. Overall POC 4–6 weeks.

[09:32] Dana: We want to test embedding parity for our vector search. What's the workflow?
[09:38] Priya: Provide a sample index, we'll run embeddings across your vendor models and Redwood's embeddings. We'll compute MRR/recall and provide a recommendation: transform vectors (cheap but re-index) or accept small drift and use mapping layer.

[10:05] Mark: Anything about model versioning and rollouts? We need canary and A/B.
[10:12] Jon: Console supports per-route version pinning, canary percent, automated rollback on metric regression, and traffic splitting. You can integrate your eval harness to fail canary if NRR/QA metrics fail.

[10:36] Dana: One last technical: KV cache — our triage uses a 2k token context with a stable prompt header and a small changing body. How do you manage cache invalidation?
[10:46] Priya: Redwood's KV cache keys on prefix hashes; when stable headers persist we only send deltas. Cache invalidation can be time-based or event-based and you can attach tags to flush particular user sessions.

[11:12] Mark: Are there migration scripts or SDK helpers for the most common differences?
[11:18] Priya: Yes — SDK adapters for function calling, a prompt transformation script for stop sequences/system-to-system mappings, and an embedding reindexing helper. We'll share links in the follow-up.

[11:36] Omar: A couple security questions to follow-up with, like encryption in transit for internal networks, and whether we can rotate keys without downtime.
[11:44] Alex: yes, we support TLS everywhere and key rotation with zero-downtime for the KMS-backed variants. We'll provide architecture docs.

[12:00] [Wrapping up]
[12:05] Alex: Quick recap — action items: we'll run the benchmark, share pricing & security pack, customer supplies sample data, and schedule a security deep-dive. Any other blockers?
[12:16] Mark: none from us. We'll aim to get the samples up by monday.
[12:21] Sofia: i'll coordinate calendars for the security call.
[12:25] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. Priya will run the bench and send results, alex will follow-up with docs.

[12:34] Dana: Thanks all.
[12:36] [Call ends]

Notes on transcription quality: multiple overlaps, a brief segment where speaker id became generic "Speaker 3", a few words mis-transcribed (e.g., gpt-4o-ish transcribed oddly).
